title: How to Bake Sourdough Crackers on a Sheet Pan
meta_description: Learn how to bake sourdough crackers on a sheet pan with step‑by‑step tips, perfect timing, and the best use of silicone baking mats for crisp, non‑stick result
html:
If you’re looking to bake sourdough crackers that are crisp, flavorful, and easy to clean up, you’re in the right place. Using a sheet pan and a good silicone baking mat makes the process simple and mess‑free, while letting the natural tang of your starter shine through.

Why a Sheet Pan Works Best for Baking Sourdough Crackers

A sheet pan provides a flat, even surface that ensures uniform heat distribution. Unlike a deep baking dish, the thin metal lets the crackers bake quickly and develop that coveted snap. Pair the pan with a silicone baking mat and you eliminate the need for parchment, reduce sticking, and enjoy zero‑scrub cleanup after you’re done.

Gathering Your Ingredients and Tools

Before you preheat the oven, assemble the essentials. This list keeps you from scrambling mid‑batch:

  • 1 cup active sourdough starter (fed and bubbly)
  • 1 ½ cups all‑purpose flour
  • ¼ cup cold unsalted butter, cut into cubes
  • ½ teaspoon sea salt
  • Optional flavor boosters: rosemary, sesame seeds, cracked pepper, grated parmesan
  • Silicone Baking Mats (non‑stick, reusable mats that replace parchment)
  • Rolling pin, sharp knife or pizza cutter, and a cooling rack

Step‑by‑Step: Baking Sourdough Crackers on a Sheet Pan

1. Preheat and prepare. Set the oven to 350°F (175°C). Place a silicone baking mat on a full‑size sheet pan. The mat’s non‑stick surface means you won’t need extra oil or parchment, and it wipes clean with a quick rinse.

2. Combine the dough. In a mixing bowl, whisk together the flour and salt. Add the cold butter and cut it into the dry ingredients until the mixture resembles coarse crumbs. Stir in the sourdough starter until a shaggy dough forms. If the dough feels too sticky, add a tablespoon of flour at a time.

3. Chill the dough. Wrap the dough in plastic wrap and refrigerate for 30 minutes. Chilling relaxes gluten and makes rolling easier, which is crucial for thin, crisp crackers.

4. Roll and cut. Lightly flour a clean surface, then roll the dough to about 1/8‑inch thickness. The thinner the roll, the crunchier the final cracker. Transfer the rolled sheet onto the silicone mat, then score it into squares or use a pizza cutter for uniform shapes.

5. Add toppings. Brush the tops lightly with olive oil (optional) and sprinkle your chosen seasonings. The silicone mat’s non‑stick nature ensures toppings stay where you place them.

6. Bake. Slide the pan into the oven and bake for 12‑15 minutes, watching closely after 10 minutes. The edges should turn golden brown; the centers will still look pale but will firm up as they cool.

7. Cool and store. Let the crackers rest on the sheet pan for 5 minutes, then move them to a cooling rack. Once completely cooled, store in an airtight container for up to a week. The silicone mat can be tossed into the dishwasher or washed by hand for next‑time use.

Tips for Perfectly Crisp and Flavorful Crackers

Even with a straightforward recipe, a few tweaks can elevate your crackers:

  • Thin is tasty. Aim for 1/8‑inch or thinner; thicker pieces stay soft.
  • Even spacing. Leave a small gap between cuts on the mat to allow steam to escape.
  • Watch the color. Because the silicone mat conducts heat well, crackers can go from golden to burnt quickly. Rotate the pan halfway through baking if your oven has hot spots.
  • Season shortly before baking. Adding herbs or seeds at the last minute prevents them from burning.

Cleaning Up Without the Hassle

The biggest win of using silicone baking mats is the cleanup. After the oven cools, simply scrape off any crumbs, rinse the mat, and it’s ready for the next batch. No parchment to toss, no greasy pans to scrub. This reusable option not only saves money but also reduces kitchen waste.

FAQ

Can I use whole‑grain flour instead of all‑purpose?

Yes. Whole‑grain flour adds nuttiness and a denser texture. You may need a bit more water to bring the dough together, and the crackers might bake a couple of minutes longer.

Do silicone baking mats work at high temperatures?

Silicone baking mats are safe up to 450°F (232°C), so 350°F for crackers is well within their range. They won’t melt or release chemicals, making them a reliable substitute for parchment.

How long can I keep the sourdough starter active for this recipe?

Maintain your starter with regular feedings (at least once a week if refrigerated). As long as it’s bubbly and smells pleasantly yeasty, it will work perfectly for baking sourdough crackers.
